summary.text: Sarah Elfreth is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Maryland's 3rd Congressional District and won re-election on November 3, 2026.
She worked in university and nonprofit advocacy before serving in the Maryland Senate from 2019 to 2025 and was first elected to Congress in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Elfreth was born in New Jersey in 1988 and, according to her congressional website, was raised by two civil servants in a union household.
She earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Towson University in 2010 and a master's degree in public policy from Johns Hopkins University in 2012.
Her congressional website says her public service began on the University System of Maryland Board of Regents.

She worked as government affairs director for the National Aquarium in Baltimore, as an adjunct professor at Towson University's Honors College, and as senior director of university projects with Margrave Strategies.

Elfreth was elected to the Maryland Senate in 2018 and served from 2019 to 2025; her congressional website says she was the youngest woman ever elected to the chamber and that 91 bills she sponsored became law.
In 2024 she won the general election for the open 3rd District seat with 59.3% of the vote.
In Congress she serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the Natural Resources Committee, where she is Vice-Ranking Member, and she sits on the Naval Academy Board of Visitors.
She won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 74.7% of the vote and, according to her congressional website, lives in Annapolis with her husband, Eric.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election with 67.3% of the vote to Berney Flowers's 32.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
